title: Israeli Diaspora minister holds talks with Austria's right-wing FPÖ
description: Israeli Diaspora Affairs and Combating Antisemitism Minister Amichai Chikli on Monday held talks in Vienna with the Freedom Party of Austria (FPÖ), the right-wing party said. Israel had long boycotted the FPÖ, which was founded by former Nazis in the 1950s. Chikli met at the Austrian Parliament with Harald Vilimsky, who heads the FPÖ delegation in the European Parliament, and National Council President Walter Rosenkranz. In a German-language post on X, Vilimsky called the talks "cordial and very informative." "It is a joy and an honor for me to be able to accompany him," he wrote. Vilimsky noted that the FPÖ had announced in Strasbourg that it would back the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA) working definition of antisemitism. Antisemitism today is "almost entirely imported or left-wing," Vilimsky said. Chikli and Vilimsky were joined by Eli Rosen, president of the Jewish Community for Styria, Salzburg and Carinthia, and Knesset lawmaker Ariel Kallner. Kallner, a member of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party, chairs the Knesset Delegation for Relations with the European Parliament. title: Israel Weapon Industries, Dutch firm to produce firearms in Netherlands
description: Israel Weapon Industries (IWI) and Dutch defense company Artillerie Inrichtingen Armaments (AIA) plan to produce two IWI firearms at a new factory in the Netherlands, the companies announced on Monday. Under the planned cooperation, the Dutch company will manufacture and assemble IWI's Arad 5 rifle and the Negev UX light machine gun. IWI will provide the technology, product expertise and manufacturing know-how. AIA will set up the Dutch manufacturing operation and the infrastructure to deliver and support the weapons. The companies said the move would lay a foundation for long-term domestic production in the Netherlands. "A strong Dutch industrial base is fundamental to national security," said AIA CEO Gerard Zondervan. Ronen Hamudot, vice chairman of IWI's parent company, SK Group, said the cooperation would bring his company's "decades of experience developing and manufacturing weapon platforms for demanding operational environments into a new industrial setting." IWI is the main supplier to the Israel Defense Forces and the Israel Police. The company said its products are used in more than 60 countries.

title: New analysis challenges Gaza famine, casualty claims using Hamas-run ministry data

The findings, published by the Australia/Israel & Jewish Affairs Council (AIJAC) on Oct. 27, were highlighted by The Washington Free Beacon on Wednesday. The figures indicated natural population growth of approximately 1.2% in 2025, with 50,227 births and 24,650 registered deaths, including 5,780 classified as nonviolent. AIJAC argued that the mortality figures contradicted the United Nations-backed Integrated Food Security Phase Classification's August 2025 famine assessment, which also relied on malnutrition and food insecurity data. Of the 24,650 recorded deaths, 18,085, or 73.4%, were male, compared with 6,565 female deaths, or 26.6%. AIJAC said the figures challenged widely circulated claims that women and children accounted for 70% of casualties, although the breakdown did not establish how many of those killed were combatants. Israel's Foreign Ministry amplified the findings, saying that Hamas's figures were “not a reliable source.” Israeli Ambassador to the European Union Avi Nir-Feldklein also denounced accusations against Israel, writing, “The Genocide lie. The Apartheid lie.” He accused Israel's critics of seeking to demonize the Jewish state and obscure Hamas's crimes. The figures used by media to shape the global debate over Gaza have frequently come from Hamas’s own Ministry of Health. "The exception—if a letter is submitted bearing the signatures of a majority of MKs (at least 61 MKs) requesting to elect a speaker at an earlier date." "We will respect the Knesset members, and if a majority of them ask to hold such a debate, I will set it for an early date and no later than a week," he continued. "There will be no clinging to the horns of the altar," he wrote, using a Hebrew expression for refusing to give up power. "You can stop promoting conspiracy theories in the media." Yisrael Beytenu and The Democrats have sent Ohana letters asking him to put the election of a new speaker on the agenda of the 26th Knesset's first session on Tuesday, Hebrew media reported. The parties reportedly remain split over who should replace Ohana. Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad has proposed outgoing Opposition Leader Yair Lapid, the party's No. 2. Rabbi Menachem Margolin, chairman of the Brussels-based European Jewish Association, wrote on X: “We stand with the congregation and call on the authorities to establish what happened. Everyone should be able to enter a place of worship without fear.” Unia, Belgium’s equality body, received 192 reports of antisemitism in 2025. That was down from 277 in 2024 but up from 121 in 2023. Annual tallies in the two years before that were below 100. Belgium’s Jewish population fell from slightly more than 41,000 in 1980 to an estimated 28,900 in 2021, a drop of nearly 30%, according to a 2022 report by the Institute for Jewish Policy Research. The study found that Belgium had fewer Jews than it did in 1946, immediately after the Holocaust.

One user amplified by Polanski suggested that the March torching of ambulances belonging to a Jewish group in London was a “false flag.” The term is used to claim that Jews or Israel staged an attack to portray themselves as victims or to justify war. title: Hebrew University of Jerusalem presents honorary fellowship to philanthropist Dr. Wallace Weber
description: The Hebrew University of Jerusalem presented an honorary fellowship to Dr. Wallace Weber during its 89th Board of Governors Meeting on Oct. 19 in Jerusalem. Weber is a retired dermatologist whose specialty practice expanded to include several offices throughout Kansas. He previously served in the Gulf War as a flight surgeon with the 82nd Airborne Division, later commanding the 410th U.S. Army Reserve Evacuation Hospital in Topeka. He retired from the U.S. Army after 31 years of service with awards including the Southwest Asia Service Medal and the Legion of Merit. Weber supports scholarships and regenerative agriculture at the Hebrew University's Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment, as well as other initiatives. He held a volunteer faculty appointment within the dermatology division at the University of Kansas School of Medicine, where he also created and endowed the university's annual lectureship, Military and Catastrophic Medicine. Weber was commissioned as a second lieutenant through the ROTC program at Colorado State University in 1965. He earned his medical degree from the University of Kansas School of Medicine in 1969. Professor Tamir Sheafer, president of the Hebrew University, bestowed the fellowship with the following citation: "in recognition of his long-standing support of Israel and the Hebrew University; in acknowledgement of his deep commitment to agricultural research and regenerative agriculture; in appreciation of his contribution to a safer world through many years of military service; in esteem for his remarkable career as a medical doctor and as an academic; in praise of his tireless efforts on behalf of the Hebrew University in the United States; and in deep gratitude for his generous donations to student scholarships and water research at the Hebrew University’s Robert H. Smith Faculty of Agriculture, Food and Environment." In accepting the honor, Weber stated, “It is an incredible and unexpected honor to be recognized by such a prestigious institution of higher learning as the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It is with much satisfaction and fondness for the accomplished members and staff of AFHU, as well as the staff, faculty and administration of the Jerusalem and Rehovot facilities, that I can reflect on my support journey over several decades.” Weber added, “It all started with a suggestion by one of the members of AFHU. The warmth and enthusiasm demonstrated in the initial contact with Beth McCoy [AFHU’s previous CEO] will ever be fond in my memory. Her staff’s ever-present willingness to help problem-solve and make me feel valued as a member of AFHU plays a major role in my support of this institution.”

description: Yashar Party leader Gadi Eisenkot addressed Israel’s friends in the United States and around the world in an X post on Wednesday, vowing to “renew and deepen” the partnership with Washington if he gets the mandate to form a government. “The Israeli people have voted for change and to replace the current government,” Eisenkot wrote in English. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc won 53 seats in the Oct. 27 Knesset election. The Zionist opposition parties—Yashar, B’Yachad (Together), The Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu—won 48. The Arab Joint List and Ra’am together secured 19 seats, leaving neither bloc with the 61 seats needed for a Knesset majority. Eisenkot said he was working to form “a national emergency government” as soon as possible. He vowed to strengthen the “bipartisan foundations” of U.S.-Israel ties, adding that Jerusalem would remain “one of America’s most reliable and capable strategic partners in the Middle East.” Eisenkot said he looks forward to working “closely and constructively” with U.S. President Donald Trump and his administration. Trump endorsed Netanyahu on Oct. 18, nine days before the election, and again on Oct. 26, the eve of the vote. In his Oct. 18 endorsement , Trump explicitly linked further American action against Iran to Netanyahu’s re-election. “If Israel has the wrong Leader, which would be anyone other than Bibi, America will have to do this work ourselves, and I am not inclined to do so,” he wrote. To all our friends in the United States and around the world: The Israeli people have voted for change and to replace the current government. Our democracy remains strong and vibrant. Double-envelope ballots are cast by Israel Defense Forces personnel, diplomats, hospital patients and other eligible voters who cannot vote at their assigned polling stations. Each ballot is sealed in a second envelope bearing the voter's details. Election officials use this to confirm that no one voted twice. The inner envelopes are then removed and mixed together to protect ballot secrecy. They are counted at a facility in the Knesset parking garage. title: Irish man gets suspended sentence for threatening Jews in France
description: An Irish man was handed a suspended sentence of six months in prison for threatening to kill a Jewish person near Marseille in August, French media reported on Tuesday. The man, identified in La Provence and other French media as Patrick O’Brien, 60, was filmed in Avignon in August telling an Australian Jewish couple that he regretted Adolf Hitler had not “finished the job,” expressing hope for Hitler's return and threatening to shoot the woman in the head. He admitted intending to hurt the couple verbally after realizing that the man was Jewish. In court, he described himself as a “great humanist,” La Provence said. The Avignon court convicted him of glorifying crimes against humanity and making death threats aggravated by antisemitic prejudice. He was ordered to pay €500 ($556) to each victim and €300 ($333) to several civil-party organizations. The court rejected prosecutors' request to ban him from French territory for three years. A lawyer representing the victims, Annie Cohen, said the sentence was excessively lenient, La Provence reported, noting that the woman's father was a Holocaust survivor. The incident had attracted widespread attention in France after a video of the confrontation went viral in August.

title: Netherlands to boycott Eurovision 2027 over Israel's participation
description: The Netherlands is set to sit out the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest because of Israel’s participation, Dutch public broadcaster NPO announced on Tuesday. The announcement follows an earlier decision to return to the event after a one-year absence over the same issue. NPO chairwoman Jet de Ranitz said discussions with broadcasters had initially suggested that a Dutch entry was possible, but efforts to reach an agreement had failed. “Because of the sensitivities surrounding the issues currently at play, we have decided to take a step back,” she said, according to NOS , a major news broadcaster affiliated with NPO. The decision followed criticism of Israel’s military operations in Gaza. Several European broadcasters have called for Israel’s exclusion. In August, Dutch broadcaster AVROTROS announced it would boycott Eurovision for a second consecutive year, arguing that the competition could no longer be considered politically neutral. NPO said it would look into tasking a different broadcaster with organizing Dutch official participation in the event. However, the plan encountered significant resistance within the NPO's constituent bodies. Earlier this month, more than 400 NPO employees signed a letter protesting participation alongside Israel. The European Broadcasting Union, which organizes Eurovision, expressed regret over the Dutch decision but said it respected the broadcaster’s position, NOS reported. Ireland has also announced that it will boycott Eurovision in 2027, citing the humanitarian situation in Gaza. Unlike the Netherlands, Ireland will not broadcast the event. Israel finished second at the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna, which was won by Bulgaria’s Dara.
author: JNS Staff

Otzma Yehudit cited heavy crowding and unusually long wait times at polling stations across the Jewish state. The Central Elections Committee said high nationwide turnout "across all sectors of society" showed "strong public engagement in the democratic process." The committee said every voter who reaches a polling station by its closing time will be able to vote.

title: German Jews fear antisemitism at France-inspired rallies
description: Germany's main Jewish umbrella group warned on Monday of a possible escalation during protests planned in the country for Oct. 31, inspired by demonstrations in France. In a statement , the Council described a “heightened threat level” over the weekend. The Council said it had indications that the planned mobilizations could turn violent, possibly against Jews. Organizers of the protests have used on social media rhetoric such as “Purge,” “like in France” and “No rules,” the Council said. The planned protests, it said, must be clearly distinguished from ordinary commercial Halloween events. Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Hanover, Dortmund, Essen, Bielefeld are among the cities where the Council identified plans for at-risk protests. "The combination of a general willingness to engage in violence, the infiltration of protests by pro-Palestinian extremists, and links to criminal networks poses a significant risk that the situation could escalate into antisemitic violence," the Council wrote.

title: 'Jews out of European countries' spray-painted in Rome
description: Unidentified parties spray-painted an antisemitic slogan on a residential building in Rome on Sunday, according to city officials and members of the local Jewish community. The graffiti that appeared on the home in Rome’s Monteverde neighborhood read "Jews out of European countries," accompanied by two Celtic crosses—a neo-Nazi symbol—according to the Italian-Jewish news site Shalom . The site quoted a police spokesperson who said the incident is under investigation. Elio Tomassetti, a local politician in charge of the district, condemned the incident, calling the graffiti "a shameful act and an act that must be punished," Shalom reported . "Precisely in a neighborhood that has been characterized by its fight against fascism, these attacks on memory have no place," he stated. Monteverde, in the Italian capital’s west, was an important center of antifascist activity during the dictatorship of Benito Mussolini and the German occupation of Rome. We strongly condemn the antisemitic and neo-fascist graffiti discovered in Rome’s Monteverde neighbourhood over the weekend. title: AIG Ireland executive exits firm amid antisemitic posts probe
description: A former insurance executive in Ireland’s branch of the AIG firm who said his social media account had been hacked and used to vilify Jews is no longer with the company, his former boss recently told local Jews last week. AIG Ireland’s president and chief executive, Eric Andersen, informed the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland (JRCI) in an email of his firm’s parting of ways with John Gillick, former head of consumer marketing and sponsorship, The Irish Times reported on Sunday. Under Gillick’s account on X, text appeared last month that described Israel and Jews as “human scum” and Jews as “filthy dogs,” according to the report. One post stated: “Jews in Ireland need to be thrown out. They are traitors and land thieves. Our children need to be educated more about how evil Israel and Jews are,” and, “no one should associate with murdering jew war criminals.” On Sept. 2, a post on the account read: “I want to let people know that my account has been compromised by unauthorised person(s) and that recent posts containing anti-Semitic content were not written, published or endorsed by me,” and, “I unequivocally condemn the views expressed in those posts. They do not reflect my beliefs or values. I strongly oppose discrimination and hate in all forms.” Initially, AIG Ireland said the social media posts in question were “fraudulently published following the unauthorised compromise of an employee’s personal social media account.” However, in informing JCRI of Gillick’s departure, Andersen wrote that matter of the posts was the subject of an ongoing police investigation, and an internal one at AIG Ireland. JRCI Chair Orli Degani told The Irish Times that she did not know the circumstances surrounding Gillick’s departure, but welcomed AIG’s investigation, the newspaper reported.

title: Jewish Choral Conducting Institute graduates first cohort of fellows
description: The Jewish Choral Conducting Institute (JCCI), a program dedicated to high-level training of conductors of Jewish choral music, has graduated its first cohort of fellows. JCCI was created by Maestro Matthew Lazar, founder and director of the Zamir Choral Foundation, to provide professional education and pass on the tradition and experience of Jewish choral music to the next generation. The fully funded institute is made possible by a major gift from Cantor Robert Lieberman and Rabbi Vicki Lieberman. Each JCCI cohort is composed of 11-15 conducting students from around the world. During the immersive two-year program, fellows attend intensive in-person retreats, workshops and monthly online meetings and receive one-on-one mentoring sessions with Lazar and guest presenters. Lazar brings knowledge of Jewish and Western music and a deep understanding of the relationship between text and music that defines choral music. He models, encourages and nurtures the talents of a new generation of conductors of Jewish music. "The conductor integrates music, text and cultural identity with mastery and precision, creating inspiring and transformative musical moments," Lazar said. "The institute provides the specialized skills and knowledge needed to make all this possible." The inaugural group of fellows has completed the program. They were presented with a certificate in Jewish Choral Conducting and performed in a recital at the North American Jewish Choral Festival. The graduates are Shani Chamovitz, Abram Foster, Joshua Gonzalez, Matthew Gonzalez, Joel Herman, Dor Kaminka, Juliana Rappaport, Elliot Roman, Yoel Rubinstein, Nitzan Shohaam and Hadas Sturman. A new cohort of JCCI fellows recently began the program, continuing the mission to share the legacy of Jewish choral music with the next generation. "We are guided by a vision of vibrant Jewish identity through the study and performance of Jewish music at the highest level of excellence. Our goal is to create a pipeline of talented and knowledgeable conductors of Jewish choral music who will ensure the future of this rich and empowering art form," Lazar said. For more information, visit: www.zamirchoralfoundation.org .

Authorities also warned of possible road closures and major traffic disruptions on routes leading to and from Eilat. The storm coincides with Tuesday's Knesset election, a national day off when many Israelis traditionally go hiking. According to the Israel Meteorological Service, heavy rain, strong winds, thunderstorms and hail are expected to begin on Tuesday afternoon around Eilat, the southern Negev and Arava, before spreading north toward the Dead Sea. After a brief overnight break, heavy rain and flash flooding are expected to resume on Wednesday afternoon. Police urged the public to avoid hiking trails, desert streambeds and nonessential travel in the affected areas

"The only way out is to form a Zionist government," he told JNS. Such a coalition would exclude "anti-Zionist ultra-Orthodox parties" and Arab parties "that do not recognize Hamas as a terrorist organization," Hendel said. He said his party is the only one outside both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc of right-wing parties, which includes the haredi factions, and the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot, which includes the Arab parties. The Reservists-New Economic Party is willing to join a government with any party except haredi and Arab ones, Hendel said. Its key objectives are universal military conscription and lowering the cost of living, he said. "We believe that those who serve should also be the ones leading the country." title: Italy arrests Hamas advocate over street riots
description: Authorities in Italy last week arrested a 30-year-old academic who justified Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, massacres for allegedly organizing violent demonstrations in Milan inspired by riots in France. Youssef Siher is suspected of inciting violence for terrorist purposes, Corriere della Sera reported on Saturday. A dual citizen of Italy and Morocco, Siher was the administrator of the Instagram page “Movimento 17 Ottobre” ("October 17 Movement"), which called for demonstrations across Italy. Siher, an organizer of Palestinian anti-Israel actions of Italy, in a 2024 essay defended the Hamas-led terrorist attacks in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, the report said. He wrote in the magazine Miccia : "Few in the West were able to conceive without ifs and buts of ‘Operation Al-Aqsa Flood’ for what it was: a revolutionary act of decolonization.” "Operation Al-Aqsa Flood" is the name that Hamas gave its rampage, in which terrorists killed some 1,200 people and abducted 251 others, amid other war crimes.   Siher had no criminal record before his arrest, the report said. His wife is under investigation on suspicion of the same offenses attributed to him. The Milan clashes are part of the apparent spread of rioting that began in France several weeks ago. Italian authorities have detained more than 370 people over the weekend and arrested nine in connection with the riots, in which far-left agitators have taken to the streets along with other protesters, many of African and Middle Eastern descent, to protest a diverse range of issues, from underfunding of education to racism in society. Similar protests have begun to occur in Spain, where authorities in Barcelona detained more than 100 people over the weekend.

It is believed the graffiti was sprayed in the early hours of Tuesday, October 20," a spokesperson for Lancashire Police told the Blackpool Gazette on Friday. The bishop of Blackburn, Philip North, was among the prominent officials who condemned the incident, which police are investigating as a hate crime, the report said. North called the incident "an assault on the values of respect, dignity and freedom of religion," and called for an "unwavering rejection of antisemitism."
